sections.overview: Platyrrhinus helleri is a fruit-eating leaf-nosed bat of Central America and northern South America.
sections.identification: Older specimens identified as P. helleri included close species now recognized separately, notably P. incarum, P. angustirostris and P. fusciventris, so identification within this group may require specialist characters.
sections.habitat: It uses a range of moist and seasonally dry habitats, including evergreen, semi-deciduous and dry forests, forest edges and fruit groves.
sections.diet: Its diet is mainly fruit, especially figs and fruits of Cecropia and Acnistus; insects are eaten occasionally.
sections.behavior: It roosts in pairs or small groups in tree crowns, caves, buildings, hollow trees or foliage; whether it builds leaf tents is not consistently documented.
sections.reproduction: Breeding is generally associated with the start of the rainy season, though timing varies among local populations.
sections.ecology: As a fruit-eater, it likely transports seeds between feeding and roosting places; the IUCN account documents its use of both natural and human-modified habitats.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern, citing its broad range, presumed large population and tolerance of varied habitats.
